original_test_intent: Verify that one approved BMC account has a consistent effective privilege when represented by the OpenBMC user-manager D-Bus model and by the IPMI user table on the intended management channel, accounting for the platform's role-to-IPMI privilege translation.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC firmware, target username/object path, IPMI user ID and channel; inventory account identity without secrets; use protected console access; read the exact D-Bus privilege/role property with `busctl get-property` or equivalent rather than relying only on introspection; capture full `ipmitool user list <channel>` and map the same user by ID/name; record enabled/callin/link/IPMI-message flags when they affect effective access; normalize both representations through the approved role map; compare and preserve discrepancies without modifying accounts.
manual_activity: Engineering supplies the target-account, IPMI-channel/user-ID and role translation; the two read-only queries and normalized comparison are fully automatable.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware and OpenBMC user-manager service/object schema
Approved target username, D-Bus object encoding/path and exact privilege/role property
IPMI management channel, user ID/name mapping and relevant enabled/callin/link/auth flags
Vendor mapping from D-Bus roles such as admin/operator/user/noaccess to IPMI privilege numbers/names, including exceptions
safety_requirements: Bind D-Bus object and IPMI row to the same account without exposing unrelated account details
Use protected console credentials and trusted host identity
Read actual properties and complete target row with exit status; do not infer from interface metadata
Issue only read-only busctl/ipmitool operations and redact usernames when required
Stop on missing/duplicate account, wrong channel, ambiguous role map, permission error or conflicting identity
agent_execution_scope: Read the approved D-Bus privilege/role property and target IPMI user row
Normalize both through the supplied mapping and retain raw plus decoded values
Report other access flags separately where they alter effective privilege
Do not select root by default, enumerate secrets, change users/passwords/privileges, clear logs or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target username/object property and IPMI channel/user ID
Approve D-Bus-role-to-IPMI-privilege translation and whether auxiliary flags are acceptance data
Review any representation/effective-access mismatch and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `ipmitool user list 1` can expose the IPMI privilege, but `busctl introspect` primarily describes interfaces and the hardcoded root/channel may not be the source's intended `[user]`.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: On the verified BMC, use property-aware D-Bus read for the approved user's role and `ipmitool user list <approved-channel>` for the mapped user ID; capture complete exits/output and normalize using the vendor map.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC console, D-Bus and IPMI privilege comparison, channel-1 literal retained pending approval, Common scope and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create an identity tuple of username, D-Bus object, IPMI channel and user ID, then compare actual role/property values through a firmware-specific translation table while preserving auxiliary access flags.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact cross-interface account identity, property-level D-Bus query, channel validation, normalized role semantics and privacy-aware evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Seeing a privilege-related interface in introspection does not return a user's current value, and matching names on the wrong channel or for a different user can produce a false agreement.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: D-Bus may expose a broad role while IPMI stores per-channel maximum privilege plus separate enabled/auth flags; textual labels need not match even when effective access is equivalent.

project_override_considerations: If the BMC intentionally derives IPMI privilege from a D-Bus role asynchronously, engineering must define propagation timing and the acceptable steady-state relation. Accounts unsupported on IPMI must have an explicit expected `NO ACCESS`/absence rule rather than being treated as missing evidence by assumption.
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware plus approved target username/object/IPMI channel/user-ID mapping
busctl/ipmitool versions and complete secret-redacted stdout/stderr/exit
Actual D-Bus privilege/role property with type/value
Exact IPMI target row including privilege and approved auxiliary flags
Applied translation table and normalized comparison result

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently asks for one user's privilege to match across D-Bus and IPMI. Placeholders and channel mapping are underspecified but not contradictory.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2243 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00025-V001: approve the BMC/firmware and target username, encoded D-Bus object path/service/interface/property, IPMI channel and user ID/name mapping; define the D-Bus role-to-IPMI privilege translation including enabled/callin/link/IPMI-message flags, unsupported-account and propagation behavior; approve protected console access and account-evidence redaction.

review_improvement: Preserves the dual-interface privilege comparison while replacing root/channel/introspection shortcuts with an exact account identity and property-to-effective-access oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: D-Bus introspection shows what properties and methods an object implements, not necessarily the current property value. IPMI privilege is also channel-specific and tied to a numeric user slot, so username text alone may not identify the same effective account. A correct comparison therefore needs a four-way mapping between D-Bus object, username, IPMI user ID and channel, followed by a role translation that considers auxiliary access flags. Every operation is read-only once that map is supplied.
